Inside the package, there was a note from the seller offering a free item if I left a 5-star review and sent them an email. I'm pretty sure that's against Amazon's seller policies. They responded positively, and today I received the gift, which was another one of the same exact item. I checked the seller's ratings and saw they have over 1000 seller ratings, all positive. So it's not like they're a brand-new seller, and I can't imagine they haven't been doing this for a while. Inside today's package was a thank you for my review (even though I haven't left one) and a reminder that for all the items they sell, a 5-star review equals a free item. My question is, would it be wrong (WIBTA) if I reported them to Amazon after receiving my free item like that? If so, what should I do instead? That seems like they're trying to manipulate reviews to make their product look better. I think Amazon has policies against this because it can mislead other buyers. But in this case, I didn't leave a review. I just pretended to have done so to get the free item. So, I'm kind of participating in their scheme by taking the free item without leaving a review. Is that wrong? I guess the seller is trying to boost their ratings by offering free items. That's probably against Amazon's policies because it's not a genuine review. It's a way to manipulate the system. Now, if I report them, would that be the right thing to do? On one hand, I'm helping Amazon enforce their policies and prevent other sellers from doing the same. On the other hand, I received a free item without leaving a review, which might make me complicit in their scheme. Is it morally acceptable to report them? Or is there something wrong with me taking the free item and then reporting them? I think the key here is whether my actions are contributing to the problem or helping to solve it. If I take the free item and then report the seller, am I being hypocritical? Or am I doing the right thing by reporting the seller's violation of Amazon's policies? Also, I should consider the impact of my actions. If I report the seller, it might help Amazon to take action against them, preventing them from continuing this practice. But if I don't report them, I'm allowing them to continue offering free items for reviews, which could mislead other buyers. Another thing to think about is whether I have any obligation to report the seller. Since I'm aware of their actions and have benefited from them, do I have a responsibility to bring it to Amazon's attention? I also need to think about the potential consequences of reporting. If I report the seller, what happens to me? Could there be any negative repercussions? Probably not, since Amazon encourages reporting of policy violations. In summary, the main points are: 1. The seller is offering free items for 5-star reviews, which is against Amazon's policies. 2. I participated by taking the free item without leaving a review. 3. Reporting the seller could help Amazon enforce their policies and prevent others from being misled. 4. Is it morally acceptable to report them, or is there something wrong with my actions? I think the morally acceptable action would be to report the seller because it helps maintain the integrity of Amazon's review system and prevents others from being misled. Even though I took the free item, reporting the seller is the right thing to do because it addresses the underlying issue.
